drills.q: Name the five forces and one AI-era example of each.
drills.a: Supplier: model API vendor controls COGS. Buyer: enterprise contracts vs zero-switching consumers. Substitutes: users reading the doc themselves instead of your summaries. Entrants: funded team cloning in <8 weeks. Rivalry: five competitors shipping near-identical features on the same base models.

drills.q: Run the attacker test on 'our chatbot is better because we fine-tuned.'
drills.a: Fails unless training data is structurally scarce: a funded competitor replicates fine-tuning in weeks if data is scrapeable/synthetic-replaceable. Passes only with hard-to-replicate data feeding a real improvement loop (e.g., years of per-student mastery traces).

drills.q: Compute: build = 3 eng-months + $6.5K/mo run; vendor = $2.4K/mo, exit 1 eng-month. 3-year horizon at $30K/eng-month loaded.
drills.a: Build: 3 x ~$120K (at $30K/mo... using 160h x rate) + run 6.5K x 36 = roughly $360K+234K = ~$594K. Buy: 2.4K x 36 = $86K + exit ~$120K = ~$206K. BUY - commodity component, cheap exit, no moat contribution.

drills.q: Draw a mini Wardley map for a RAG product; identify one play.
drills.a: Need: trusted answers from private docs. Chain: chat UI (product) -> orchestration (custom->product fast) -> retrieval (commodity-ish) -> embeddings (utility) -> generation (utility). Plays: open-source the orchestrator to commoditize competitors' chains while differentiating on eval harness; or compliance-wrapped deployment exploiting enterprise inertia.

drills.q: CEO fears '[Cloud Giant] will clone us.' Give the serious assessment checklist.
drills.a: Distribution? Data loop (years of usage traces)? Workflow embedment/migration friction for installed users? Incentive (market big enough AND non-cannibalizing)? Track record of maintaining keynote categories after 18 months? Score honestly: real risk -> differentiate into workflow/trust layers now; noise -> stop relitigating.

drills.q: Should a mid-size company self-host open-weight models? The economics.
drills.a: Usually no below scale: serving engineering + GPU ops ~= several engineers fully loaded (~$1M+/yr) versus API prices falling ~10x per 18-24 months (drift against you). Cross-over cases: extreme privacy constraints, predictable giant volume, latency-critical edge inference.

drills.q: Vendor announces 5x price increase on a core dependency. Playbook?
drills.a: Quantify COGS exposure in unit-economics terms; invoke contract terms; negotiate with credible alternative as leverage; activate pre-priced exit plan (abstraction layer = weeks not quarters); then log into ledger process - diversify where cheap via dual-provider interfaces, accept where switching costs exceed expected repeat-shock losses.

drills.q: Your product's users start scripting against internal endpoints. Platform now?
drills.a: Not yet automatically: verify pull evidence volume (unsolicited integrations, partner inquiries), test toll enforceability (metering/billing/ToS), accept platform tax consciously (compat forever, slower iteration). Without builder density ship product-with-clean-API plus private partner integrations; formalize when partners outnumber your own roadmap items.

drills.q: New AI-compliance obligations land 2026-2027. Threat or opportunity for an incumbent? A challenger?
drills.a: Incumbent: opportunity disguised as burden - costs amortize across revenue, raising entry barriers around installed base. Challenger: compliance-forward positioning in risk-sensitive segments (health/finance/education) where buyers pay premiums for certified boringness. Both: build evidence pipelines once (eval logs, docs, incident response) as reusable moat input.

drills.q: 'Our AI assistant began as a feature - when does it deserve business-level investment?'
drills.a: When it shows independent retention (users return specifically for it), standalone-attributable unit economics (own activation funnel, measurable willingness-to-pay), and a defensible wedge. Until then it borrows the parent's moat and shouldn't pay business-team prices - funding it as one creates an orphaned team that neither moves the host nor survives alone.
